asr_text: A useful way to use the slider is to ask one question: Am I trying to keep water in, or let a gas out? If the main problem is wilting, a high humidity is the better match. Leafy greens such as kale and broccoli can lose water quickly, so a more closed drawer can help. If the main problem is gas, low humidity may be the better match. Apples and pears give off ethylene, a gas that can make nearby produce ripen too quickly. More air movement helps that gas escape. This turns the slider into a simple diagnosis tool. You do not have to memorize a fruit and vegetable rule. You can look at the food's main storage problem.

When people imagined getting a full month off, the most common answer was a trip of about one week. It was chosen by about 24%. This shows that many people can imagine giving travel more time when the chance exists.

I want my work and things to have a place, even when I cannot choose the desk rules.
